summary: Introduces delegation: by default tasks run on hosts matching the play's `hosts`, but you can delegate tasks or facts to other machines or run playbooks locally. Example: removing webservers from a load balancer by delegating to localhost.
questions: How do I run one task on a different machine than the play's hosts?
How can I pull a webserver out of the load balancer during an update?
Can I run a playbook locally instead of over SSH?

answer_card.title: Controlling where tasks run
answer_card.answer_md: By default Ansible gathers facts and runs all tasks on the hosts matching the play's `hosts` line. You can instead delegate a task to another machine or group, delegate facts, or run an entire playbook locally. For example, when updating webservers you can delegate the "remove from load balancer pool" task to localhost, keeping everything in one play.
